# Extraction prompt v1 (extract_v1) — template

You are labelling one end-of-day review chart of the S&P 500 Emini (5-minute bars,
one full US session) for a personal research dataset. The chart is annotated by
price-action trader Al Brooks: blue title bar, coloured signal-bar boxes, dotted
trend/channel lines, and handwritten-style pattern notes.

## What to output

A single JSON object matching the label schema (DayLabel v1). No prose, no fences.

## How to read the chart (rules)

1. Read ONLY what is annotated or visibly evident. Do not infer unseen bars.
2. `day_type`: use one canonical id from the taxonomy below (or `other`).
3. `events`: one entry per visible annotation. `label` must be a canonical event id;
   if the wording has no canonical match, set `label` to null and keep the exact
   wording in `raw_label` (never drop it, never force a wrong id).
4. Times: read `HH:MM` from the chart axis (US Pacific). Store `{"time": "HH:MM",
   "tz": "America/Los_Angeles"}`. Omit times you cannot read (null).
5. `outcome`: judge success/fail only when the chart shows what happened after the
   event; else `unclear` with an `outcome_reason`.
6. `confidence`: 0..1 per day type and per event. List genuinely uncertain items
   with low confidence rather than guessing.
7. `evidence`: name the supporting text/graphic (e.g. "blue title bar",
   "red box on 10:35 bar", "dotted wedge lines").
8. `image_id` and `date` are given below — copy them exactly.
9. `extraction_meta`: {"provider": <given>, "model_id": <given>,
   "prompt_version": "extract_v1"}.

## Few-shot examples (textual, from reviewed charts)

Example A — 29 Jul 2022 (Spike and Channel Bull Trend):
day_type=spike_and_channel_bull (0.9). Events: spike (bull, morning, success),
channel (bull, midday, success), buy_the_close (bull, 12:55 PT, success,
evidence "Buy The Close note + strong last bars").

Example B — 1 Aug 2022 (Bull Trend From The Open, Then Trading Range):
day_type=bull_trend_from_open (0.7, note the afternoon range in session_summary).
Events: spike (bull, success), trading_range_begin/trading_range_end (neutral,
times from axis), failed_breakout (bear attempt midday, fail).

## Taxonomy and schema

Appended after this template by the pipeline (canonical ids + field reference).


## Taxonomy v1 (canonical ids only)

Day types: bear_trend_from_open, broad_bear_channel, broad_bull_channel, bull_trend_from_open, other, reversal_day, small_pullback_bear_trend, small_pullback_bull_trend, spike_and_channel_bear, spike_and_channel_bull, trading_range, trend_reversal_to_bear, trend_reversal_to_bull, trending_trading_range

Events: bear_flag, body_gap, breakout, bull_flag, buy_the_close, channel, channel_line_overshoot, climax, double_bottom, double_top, ema_gap_bar, entry_bar, exhaustive_climax, failed_breakout, failed_signal, final_flag, gap, h1, h2, higher_low_double_bottom, l1, l2, lower_high_double_top, major_bear_surprise, major_bull_surprise, measured_move, micro_double_bottom, micro_double_top, opening_reversal, pullback_50pct, sell_the_close, signal_bar, spike, trading_range_begin, trading_range_end, trend_line_break, truncated_wedge, wedge

Day-type synonyms: bear trend from open -> bear_trend_from_open, bear trend from the open -> bear_trend_from_open, broad bear channel -> broad_bear_channel, broad bull channel -> broad_bull_channel, bull trend from open -> bull_trend_from_open, bull trend from the open -> bull_trend_from_open, small pullback bear trend -> small_pullback_bear_trend, small pullback bull trend -> small_pullback_bull_trend, spike and channel bear trend -> spike_and_channel_bear, spike and channel bull trend -> spike_and_channel_bull, trading range day -> trading_range, trend reversal to bear -> trend_reversal_to_bear, trend reversal to bull -> trend_reversal_to_bull

Event synonyms: 50 percent pullback -> pullback_50pct, 50% pullback -> pullback_50pct, bear flag -> bear_flag, body gap -> body_gap, btc -> buy_the_close, bull flag -> bull_flag, buy the close -> buy_the_close, channel line overshoot -> channel_line_overshoot, db -> double_bottom, double bottom -> double_bottom, double top -> double_top, dt -> double_top, ema gap bar -> ema_gap_bar, entry bar -> entry_bar, exhaustive climax -> exhaustive_climax, failed breakout -> failed_breakout, failed signal -> failed_signal, final flag -> final_flag, higher low double bottom -> higher_low_double_bottom, hl db -> higher_low_double_bottom, lh dt -> lower_high_double_top, lower high double top -> lower_high_double_top, major bear surprise -> major_bear_surprise, major bull surprise -> major_bull_surprise, measured move -> measured_move, micro double bottom -> micro_double_bottom, micro double top -> micro_double_top, mm -> measured_move, opening reversal -> opening_reversal, sell the close -> sell_the_close, signal bar -> signal_bar, stc -> sell_the_close, trading range begin -> trading_range_begin, trading range end -> trading_range_end, trend line break -> trend_line_break, truncated wedge -> truncated_wedge

## Output schema (DayLabel v1, strict)

Top-level: schema_version=1, image_id, date (YYYY-MM-DD), day_type, day_type_confidence (0..1), session_summary, events[], extraction_meta.
Event: label (canonical event id or null) + raw_label (verbatim, required when label is null), direction (bull|bear|neutral), start_time/end_time ({time HH:MM, tz}), bar_index_hint, price_hint, outcome (success|fail|partial|unclear), outcome_reason, confidence (0..1), evidence, source (vision|human|engine).
